conclusions.rationale: Observable UI list operations (add/remove, pointer and keyboard reorder), restart persistence and rejection of duplicate/empty identities without partial write are testable; Story 1 and the has_validation/is_keyboard_navigable traits give concrete scenarios.

source_citations.excerpt: supports add/remove and both pointer and keyboard reorder, and preserves the exact committed order after restart
Duplicate or empty device identities are rejected without a partial write.
Persist a unique ordered list of microphone choices

conclusions.rationale: Status vocabulary is closed (available/unavailable/ambiguous/unknown), refresh triggers are quantified (open, every 5 seconds, manual Retry), and effective-device display rules cover active, last-used and after-restart cases. FR-002 separates unknown enumeration from disappearance.

source_citations.excerpt: Availability refreshes when the audio settings open, every 5 seconds while they remain open, and on manual Retry
otherwise the device used by the last recording since launch, labelled as such, or "not used yet" after a restart
failed enumeration is unknown, not proof that a device disappeared

conclusions.rationale: Ordered resolution, ambiguity as a failed attempt, single re-enumeration, default-after-configured and bounded timeouts (2 s per attempt, 6 s total) are stated and measurable. The interaction between the per-attempt and total bound when several attempts time out is recorded as a non-critical ambiguity below; it does not prevent testing either bound.

source_citations.excerpt: Each open attempt times out after 2 seconds and the whole resolution after 6 seconds
Attempt the system default only after configured attempts fail
with bounded attempts and explicit failure

conclusions.rationale: Retention of saved choices across fallback/disconnect/reconnect, preference for a reconnected higher-priority device at the next recording, always-on re-resolution before capture and non-interruption of the current session are explicit and consistent with FR-004 and the Clarifications on always-on edits. Supporting context outside this requirement's sections: .specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L394-L415 ('in always-on mode an edit saved during a recording reopens the stream after that recording ends').

source_citations.excerpt: A fallback, disconnect or reconnect never deletes/reorders saved choices or resets the clamshell setting.
Editing priority during a recording affects the next session and does not interrupt or discard the current session's captured audio.

conclusions.rationale: Closed-lid behavior is defined as override then system default, open/unknown lid uses the normal list, and resolution never changes settings; the empty-list scenario in is_submittable confirms override precedence.

source_citations.excerpt: with a configured override and a confirmed closed lid, attempt the clamshell microphone; if it is unavailable or fails to open, attempt the system default, as today
Preserve the existing closed-lid behavior (override first, then system default)

conclusions.rationale: The 2026-10-14 decision removes the round-1 ambiguity on the literal "default": null maps to an empty list, any non-null value including "default" maps to a one-entry list with that exact name. Key-presence gating, idempotence, retention of unavailable legacy choices, clamshell preservation and recoverability on persistence failure are testable with fixtures.

source_citations.excerpt: a non-null legacy selected_microphone becomes one priority entry with that exact name, including the device name "default"; null (the system default) becomes an empty normal priority list
Migration is idempotent, retains unavailable legacy choices, preserves clamshell settings and leaves the original store recoverable if persistence fails.
"default" is an ordinary device name (a real ALSA PCM on Linux), never a sentinel

conclusions.rationale: Shared validation/transactions between UI and CLI, single commit of the complete order, explicit errors without partial change, the stale-revision draft/Reload behavior and cache invalidation for the next stream opening are all observable.

source_citations.excerpt: On a stale revision the UI keeps the draft, shows that settings changed elsewhere and offers Reload, which displays the committed order and discards the draft.
A committed priority update invalidates cached resolution for the next stream opening without interrupting an active recording.
Share typed validation, atomic persistence, revision conflict handling, cache invalidation and setting change notifications between UI and CLI.

conclusions.rationale: The two CLI operations, JSON envelope, stable codes and absence of credentials are stated. Two 2026-10-14 decisions settle what round 1 left open: `microphones list` is a live operation that returns the 008 live-only refusal (unavailable, exit 5) without a running Handy while the configured order stays readable with `settings get microphone_priority`; and the legacy `selected_microphone` key becomes read-only, generic set refused with validation_failed/2 and details.reason microphones_domain. The error-code list in AC-008 is illustrative ('errors use the F8 stable codes'), so the added unavailable/5 refusal is consistent with it.

source_citations.excerpt: F8 offers `handy settings microphones list` (configured order, availability, effective device and reason)
errors use the F8 stable codes

`handy settings set selected_microphone …` returns `validation_failed` (exit 2) with `details.field = "selected_microphone"` and `details.reason = "microphones_domain"`

conclusions.rationale: Configured vs effective separation, unknown on enumeration failure and ambiguous handling are specific and map to AC-002/AC-003.

source_citations.excerpt: Same-named ambiguous devices are reported as ambiguous, are skipped as a failed attempt at stream opening rather than resolved to an arbitrary device, and remain saved until explicitly edited.

source_citations.excerpt: Resolve and open normal microphone choices in order, then system default, with bounded attempts and explicit failure.

conclusions.rationale: Next-opening application, session device retention, device-loss handling (keep and transcribe captured audio, notify cut short, no splicing) are explicit; Story 2 'Device lost during a recording' gives the scenario.

source_citations.excerpt: A device loss ends the current recording: audio captured before the loss is kept and transcribed normally, the user is told the recording was cut short, and no other microphone is spliced into its samples.

conclusions.rationale: Closed-lid preservation and non-erasure of settings, testable with clamshell fixtures.
